verdicts.reason: A breaks the hierarchy. The 'LONGEST DAY SALE' banner drops below the copy into the lower third, the legal line is promoted to sit right under the subhead, and the CTA shrinks to a tiny pill under the banner, leaving a big dead band under the logo. B keeps the original reading order and a strong CTA, but 'last' is orphaned on the headline's second line and the legal text crowds the subhead with a 'Co., 2026.' widow. Its CTA is also oversized and the logo sits off-centre to the right of the banner.

A has a clean centred axis, a one-line headline and a well-sized CTA. But the sale banner is shrunk into a small sticker wedged between the legal line and the CTA, losing its headline role, and the legal copy is promoted above the action. B keeps the banner prominent at the top, but the headline is broken with 'last' orphaned and the subhead, legal text and CTA are jammed together at the bottom. B's legal text also widows 'Co., 2026.', the CTA is too heavy and the logo is off-axis.
